A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same linear-time-encoder study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D are readable and support a reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic sequence-classification experiments, dynamic link-prediction results on six datasets, and dimensionality and attention analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds resource measurements, TGN/CAWN experiments, dynamic node classification, and comparative attention analyses.

M1.justification: The standardized linear encoder in Equation 1 and the TGAT, DyGFormer-separate, and DyGDecoder procedures are retained. The additional backbones and classification experiments test the existing encoder; the clarified beginning-of-sequence embedding does not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Appendix D.6 adds dynamic node classification on Wikipedia and Reddit, substantially extending real-graph task coverage beyond future link prediction. The six underlying graph datasets and the original synthetic sequence-classification task remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The attention analysis newly compares sinusoidal encoders against linear encoders, whereas v1 visualized only linear encoders. Table 9 also introduces within-backbone sinusoidal-versus-linear comparisons for TGN and CAWN, previously only discussed or cited. The main benchmark comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: The new node-classification evaluation pretrains a link-prediction backbone, freezes it, trains a classification head, and reports AU-ROC. v2 also introduces per-epoch runtime and peak-memory measurements. Existing main-experiment splits, negative sampling, AP evaluation, optimizer, and hyperparameter searches remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds runtime and memory profiling and extends attention analysis to directly test how sinusoidal and linear encodings affect learned patterns across the datasets. These substantially expand the practical-efficiency and mechanism evidence. The original dimensionality, cosine-versus-sine-cosine, waiting-time, and positional-encoding analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions specify ten runs for synthetic experiments and means and standard deviations over five runs for the main graph experiments. The added predictive-result tables continue the mean-plus/minus-variation format without introducing a new uncertainty-estimation procedure, significance test, or explicitly increased run count.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 retain their values, but v2 adds substantial results in Tables 7–10 and sinusoidal attention maps. Table 9 favors linear encoders in seven of eight TGN/CAWN comparisons; for example, TGN on UCI reports 94.53 AP with linear versus 87.00 with sinusoidal encoding. Table 10 instead favors linear for TGAT and sinusoidal for DyGFormer on both classification datasets.

T1.justification: Proposition 3.1 and its Appendix B proof are unchanged. Section 4.2.3 adds a concrete cosine construction that uniquely encodes the twelve discrete time differences in US Legis, together with a floating-point collision example for a larger time range. This is a limited addition to the mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The three central contributions remain the linear encoder, the attention-based time-span construction, and improved link prediction with parameter savings. The abstract's added acknowledgment that encoders can be combined already appeared in v1's conclusion. Additional experiments support or qualify the existing claims rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the UCI instability qualification with an interpretation emphasizing recovery under distribution shift. It adds explanations for encoder-dependent attention patterns and resource costs, expands the US Legis granularity discussion, and explicitly acknowledges mixed node-classification performance and the need for broader evaluation.

D1.justification: v2 newly reports training time and peak GPU memory, identifies the visualized attention layers as the last layers, and clarifies the learnable beginning-of-sequence embedding and fixed non-temporal channel dimensions. These improve documentation without establishing changes to the retained experiments. The code-access link remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Time2Vec and Shukla and Marlin's irregular-time-series work. Section 5 positions the encoder against Time2Vec's combined linear and periodic features, identifies standardization as a distinction, and leaves hybrid encoders for future study. The broader related-work framework is retained.

P1.justification: There are localized abstract and introduction rewrites, clearer temporal-feature terminology, expanded explanatory paragraphs, and publication-header additions. Three new appendix subsections precede the relocated attention subsection, but the overall narrative and main section structure remain stable.

P2.justification: v2 adds the architecture schematic in Figure 4 and four new experimental tables. Attention displays are substantially expanded and reorganized into encoder comparisons: Reddit becomes the main-text example, while the retained Enron and other linear-attention panels are redistributed through the appendix alongside new sinusoidal panels.

improvement.justification: The resource measurements, additional backbones, and mixed node-classification results strengthen practical support and clarify applicability beyond v1's evidence. Comparative attention plots and Time2Vec positioning also improve explanation and context. These are useful supplementary improvements to unchanged central results; limited implementation detail for the added experiments, including unspecified timing hardware, constrains their reproducibility and the overall gain.
